title: Steak Frites with Maître d' Butter
description: A pan-seared steak with twice-fried potatoes and a slice of parsley and lemon butter melting on top. Anthony Bourdain became executive chef of Brasserie Les Halles in Manhattan in 1998, and his 2004 Les Halles Cookbook is a guide to the restaurant's classic bistro cooking.
notes:
Inspired by Anthony Bourdain, *Anthony Bourdain's Les Halles Cookbook* (2004). Written for Sous; not his recipe.

The first fry can be done hours ahead; leave the blanched fries on a rack at room temperature and give them the second fry just before serving. Extra maître d' butter keeps for a week in the fridge or three months in the freezer, and is good on fish, vegetables or toast.

Hanger, flank or bavette steaks work too: cook them to medium-rare and slice across the grain.
ingredients: 2 quarts (2 L) peanut or other high-heat oil, for frying
2 boneless strip or rib-eye steaks, 10 to 12 ounces (300 to 340 g) each, about 1 inch (2.5 cm) thick
steps: Mash the butter with the parsley, lemon juice, shallot, salt and pepper until evenly mixed. Spoon onto plastic wrap, roll into a log about 1 inch across, and chill until firm, at least 30 minutes.
Cut the potatoes into sticks about 1/4 inch (6 mm) thick. Soak in cold water for 30 minutes, then drain and dry very thoroughly on towels.

Heat the oil in a heavy pot to 300°F (150°C). Fry the potatoes in two or three batches until limp and cooked through but not coloured, 5 to 6 minutes. Drain on a rack and let them rest for at least 15 minutes.
Pat the steaks dry and season with the salt and pepper. Heat a cast-iron skillet over high heat until very hot, add the oil, and lay in the steaks.

Sear without moving for 3 to 4 minutes, until a dark crust forms, then turn. Add the butter and spoon it over the steaks as they cook another 3 to 4 minutes, until an instant-read thermometer reads 125 to 130°F (52 to 54°C) for medium-rare.
Move the steaks to a board, top each with a 1/2-inch slice of the maître d' butter, and rest for 5 to 8 minutes.
# The second fry and to serve:

While the steaks rest, heat the oil to 375°F (190°C). Fry the potatoes in batches until deep golden and crisp, 2 to 3 minutes. Drain, toss with fine salt, and serve straight away next to the steaks with their melting butter.
